copy.blurb:
The model fancies Qatar more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Bosnia and Herzegovina. +16.1pp is one of the widest in the priced field; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Elo numbers going in: Bosnia and Herzegovina 1660, Qatar 1640. That's a 20-point lead for Bosnia and Herzegovina — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 38%, the draw at 29%, and Qatar to win at 34%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Qatar on the win side reads 34%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 53%, the draw at 25%, and Qatar to win at 18%. On the Qatar side specifically the market reads 18%, which prices out at American odds of +471. Compared against the model's 34%, that's the +16.1pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Qatar the lower bound is 29%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +11.2pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Qatar side specifically.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 29 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the Qatar side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Qatar a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +16.1pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
copy.summary: The model thinks Qatar are mispriced. Our number reads 34% on the away side; the market reads 18%. The +16.1pp gap is the Pick.
